category_story: mlp1 is a giant front token-table keyed on the current token's surface identity/spelling: it fires hardest on subword/compound continuations that are near-deterministic given the current token alone -- completing a word split across BPE tokens (e.g. 'six-re'->'actor', 'epitom'->'izes', 'BRU'->'CE', 'TOGET'->'HER'), repeated legal-boilerplate compounds (e.g. 'Transferor'/'Transferee'->' spouse'), and form-filler boilerplate ('Yes___No__'->'____'). Its scope is 'the next BPE fragment of an in-progress multi-token word or fixed phrase', not context-dependent selection at all.
surprises: The context ('federal Defense' -> ' of') strongly evokes 'Defense of Marriage Act' (DOMA), a very specific institutional phrase, yet the circuit responsible is the generic mlp1 token-table plus mlp16, not a specialized long-range lookup head -- 'Defense' alone is apparently enough to make ' of' the modal continuation without needing to reference anything upstream. mlp16 showing up as a secondary contributor (1.11 dCE) at a much later layer than mlp1 is new; not previously flagged in the known circuit list.
